# <a id="_Toc138762086"></a>Development and Delivery

##### Purpose of this document is to give an overview of the development process in and Kit delivery of TeamcenterX\.

##### Policy Tag

##### Siemens Industry Software \(SISW\) SaaS Secure Development Policy\.pdf

##### Scope

This document defines the overall process for development and deliver in TeamcenterX teams\. 

## <a id="_Toc138762087"></a>__Introduction__

Teamcenter X delivery comprises of Teamcenter RTM kits along with provisioning and configuration management scripts to CApS \(formerly known as Managed Services\)\. The delivered package will then be used by the CApS team to setup an Teamcenter X installation for a customer\. 

The installable artifacts of Teamcenter are not modified and are the same artifacts that gets distributed to on\-prem customers\. These installable artifacts are hosted on an AWS S3 bucket configured to have restricted access and version control\. The configuration management and provisioning scripts make use of AWS Cloud formation and Chef\. These provisioning and configuration management scripts create and install a secure stack for a given customer\. 

SAFE Agile methodology is used to prioritize backlog items, define capabilities and features, schedule, implement and deliver the prioritized capabilities through various program increments\. 

Gitlab is used as SCM tool\. Custom scripts integrated with Gitlab CI/CD pipelines build, test and to deliver Teamcenter X kits for CApS team consumption\.

## <a id="_Toc109379042"></a><a id="_Toc138762090"></a>Procedure to ensure code integrity

1. The process of generating the kits is executed through Gitlab CI/CD pipeline process \- \.gitlab\-ci\.xml\. This file defines various stages and applies rules to restrict execution of script based on the type of branch its executed from\.
2. Changes to the file needs approval from TCX Approval Group created for reviewing the code changes   before the changes are merged to the main branch\. 
3. Teamcenter kits are published to S3 bucket with restricted access and version controlled\. Read/Write access to AWS S3 bucket, tcx\-release\-management is restricted to federated users\. A federated user is a Siemens user with their webkey mapped to the AWS account\. 
4. The policy of S3 bucket has version control, access logs and encryption enabled\.
5. Provisioning and configuration management scripts, that are part of clouddeployment\.zip, are published to S3 buckets\. Development S3 bucket has read/write access to the AWS development account used for testing the deployment\.

### <a id="_Toc109379044"></a>Development \- Build and test

This process is used by development teams to perform incremental features to the Teamcenter X product as a part of the PI process\.

1. During a PI, developers of Teamcenter X perform changes as per the planned PI deliverables to their development branches\.
	1. Commit changes automatically trigger a pipeline build and a set of artifacts are built\. Artifacts generated as a part of this process are clouddeployment\.zip, cloudapps\.zip, customerinstancemanagerlambda\.zip\. This artifact generated as a part of dev\-build\-kit expires in 24 hours from the time it was built\.

2. Developer will present the code in the code review meetings scheduled for everyday 2:30 PM to 3:00 PM IST\.

### <a id="_Toc109379045"></a>Procedure for Product Validation – Build and test

Incremental changes implemented by the development will be validated by Product Validation team\. 

1. By specifying CI/CD deployment\_mode variable to __product\-validation__ a kit for PV team validation can be created\. This pipeline can only be triggered on the master branch or on tcx version specific master branch\. Triggering pipeline execution on master branches is restricted to only to Maintainer role users
2. The pipeline execution pushes the artifacts generated to a S3 bucket different from the development bucket
3. With this pipeline one tag will be created on top of the Git master branch or tcx version specific master branch with the format as below\. The same tag name will be applied to all the artifacts pushed to the S3 bucket\. A MD5 check sum of the cloud automation kit will be generated and published to the S3 bucket\. This acts as integrity check for the generated kit\. [https://aws\.amazon\.com/premiumsupport/knowledge\-center/data\-integrity\-s3/](https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/knowledge-center/data-integrity-s3/)

tcx\-DD\-Mon\-YYYY\-<BuildPipelineNumber>

For example:

tcx\-31\-Mar\-2022\-082302

![A screenshot of a computer

Description automatically generated with medium confidence](data:image/png;base64,)

1. Once the kits are generated and pushed to the PV bucket\. We send a mail to PV team for performing validation\. The mail is sent by the Git project admin\(s\)\. As part of the new process we are planning to send mail via Teams channel so that it will be recorded in a sheet kept at sharepoint\.
2. Product Validation team executes manual tests on this deployment\. They file defects on Polarion against TcX team if any issues are identified in the testing
3. On completion of the tests the environment can be deleted using delete script \\{TODO: What’s the process PV follows to delete a PV environment?\\} The PV will use pipeline and TCX cookbooks to perform deletion of stacks\.
4. Any defects filed by PV in step\#3 will need to be addressed by development and process followed will be the steps mentioned in development build and test section\.

### <a id="_Toc109379046"></a>Procedure for Dry run – Build and test

Once the validation of the product validation kits is done and the kits are ready to release then the same kits will be pushed to pre\-prod for dry run verification by CApS team\.

Dry run is not a mandatory process, and it will be decided based on the content delivered and change in the process of deployment\.

Publishing kits to Pre\-Prod is executed incrementally during the PI to give CApS team an early access of content\.

1. Maintainer role users manually triggers the pre\-prod kit creation based on discussion between development, program management and product management\.
2. Kits are pushed to a pre\-production S3 bucket for CApS consumption\.
3. CApS team performs tests and communicates with development on the issues and files defects in Polarion
4. Development works on the issues and deliver changes back to pre\-prod bucket for validation\.

## <a id="_Toc109379047"></a><a id="_Toc138762092"></a>Production Release

Trigger to production release is based on 

1. Teamcenter Release Management team delivering a Teamcenter release based on the release criteria
2. Teamcenter X team getting a signoff from PV and CApS dry run status \\{TODO: Document this process\\}
	1. By specifying CI/CD deployment mode variable to __production__ a production build for delivery to CApS team will be created\. This pipeline can only be triggered on the master branch or on tcx version specific master branch\. Triggering pipeline execution on master branches is restricted to only to TCX approval list members
	2. The kits are published to production S3 bucket

## <a id="_Toc109379048"></a><a id="_Toc138762093"></a>Git CI\-CD pipeline

### <a id="_Toc109379049"></a>Procedure for Gitlab\-ci\.yml CI\-CD code change 

The procedure of updating git ymal file is same as any other feature/defect implementation\.

Any changes in the Gitlab\-ci\.yml will according to following steps:

1. The requirements shall be generated as part of PI planning\.
2. The team member needs to submit an MR with the changes in the pipeline jobs\.
3. Developer creates merge request \(MR\) for the changes and Gitlab CI/CD pipeline automatically triggers build and unit test for these changes\. 
4. The team member will perform testing with the dev pipeline\.
5. The team member will present the code in the code review meetings 

Code review meeting:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

1. Once the review is done and all the review comments are addressed\. The MR should be approved by at least 2 of the 4 members from TCX approval group before it can be merged with the main branch

### <a id="_Toc109379050"></a>Procedure for creating Git docker image

In Teamcenter X only the docker images from chimera are used\. Custom images for any of the build jobs are not allowed\.
